name: core-loop-visual
description: Visual verification of the full core gameplay loop: survey → drill plan → charge → sequence → blast → fragments → contract delivery. Multi-angle screenshots at each phase to confirm smooth transitions and visual feedback.

steps.description: campaign start replaces the site entirely with dusty_hollow's own fixed 96x96 grid -- new_game's size:24 above never actually takes effect once this runs.

Corrected from bare positional args (`employee assign_skill 1 geology 3`), which the command silently rejects (`skill`/`level` are named params, per assignSkillCommand's own usage string) -- Finding #15's class, the same syntax bug caught earlier in survey-confidence-overlay.json. Left unmarked: hiring already grants the Rookie starting qualification (ROLE_STARTING_QUALIFICATION in Employee.ts); this only raises the level for the scenario's needs -- the player-facing path is `employee train`.
Not long enough for the surveyor to walk to (20,20) and complete the survey (arrival-gated, #437) -- this file's own core-loop demonstration doesn't wait on it, moving straight to drilling instead.

expect.note: confirmed via direct trace: cash stays flat here -- with only 1 employee and no buildings/vehicles yet, payroll doesn't cycle within just 5 ticks

steps.description: Resolved through the event dialog's own buttons. Decides whether an event is pending from authoritative game state, not from whether the modal has rendered -- a DOM-only probe silently missed events on a no-GPU runner where a frame costs ~6s, leaving them pending so later ticks halted and the run diverged while still passing command mode.

steps.command: drill_plan grid rows:4 cols:4 spacing:3 depth:6 start:20,20
steps.description: Corrected from the original rows:3 cols:3 spacing:5 (which command mode ran literally, producing 9 holes): the click drags the (20,20)-(30,30) rectangle at the Drill panel's own default spacing (DEFAULT_SPACING_M=3), computing cols/rows as round(size/spacing)+1 = 4x4 = 16 holes for that same rectangle -- the command and the click were silently testing two different grids, the same class of bug already fixed in nav-cell-types-visual.json. Caught by adding expect.equals.holeCount; fixed by describing what the click actually produces. depth corrected from 8 to 6 (Ground rule #15/Finding #42's class, the whole-suite audit before Phase 3): this step never clicks the grid tool's depth stepper (data-field="depth"), so the real drag always produces the panel's own 6m default regardless of what's declared. This file's own expect blocks only assert hole/charge/sequence counts around the affected blast (depth-insensitive), so this is a metadata-only correction -- verified both modes still pass unchanged.

This file never buys any software tier, so the preview prints '[Requires software tier N]' for every section (see safety-projection-visual.json for the unlocked version) -- still a real, clickable control either way.

BLOCKED, and deliberately not converted to a click: the ACTIVE card's DELIVER button is genuinely disabled at this point. ContractsPanel disables the amount box, MAX and DELIVER together whenever maxDeliverable = min(contract remaining, stored material) is 0, and a direct trace of this file shows 0.0 kg of dirtite in storage against a 320 kg contract -- nothing in this scenario ever hauls material into storage. The console command is no better: it returns success:false and command mode only fails a step on a thrown exception, so `contract deliver 1 amount:500` is a silent no-op in BOTH modes today. `expect.blocked` is what now pins it down -- the button must be in the DOM and refused, with `expect.usable` on the panel's own storage link proving the panel is really open, so "blocked" cannot pass just because nothing is on screen. Forcing a click here would be asserting something the game correctly forbids.

expect.note: the contract stays active/undelivered -- this file's own "contract delivery" step in its description is a queued attempt, not a completed one; economy-full-loop.json is the file that actually hauls stock and completes a delivery
